gap: No result ChatGPT got states what these CD radios cost today or whether they can be bought new. On 2026-11-08 Target sold the GPX BC112B AM/FM CD boombox for $26.49 and the Jensen CD-560 (which adds Bluetooth) for $49.99, down from $65.99. Sony's CFD-S70, which ChatGPT showed as a card, had no listing at Target or Best Buy, and the only US offer opened was a refurbished unit at $159.99.
standout_why: Compared against dailydealhere.com 'The 9 Best CD Boomboxes in 2026' (lists BC112B, CD-490, Philips AZ797T and others), bestspeakerreviews.com 'Best CD AM FM Stereo Systems' (Jensen JBS-300, Panasonic SC-PM270, Nextron, MEGATEK, Emerson) and loudersound.com (its body did not load; only the title came back). Neither page that loaded gives a single price or says whether a model is in stock. The Sony pages ChatGPT got are spec pages with no US price, and the Best Buy and Target results are bare listings. No page links prices to the trade-offs: AM or FM only, Bluetooth or not, presets or not.
decides: The cheapest model that does what the shopper typed (CD plus AM/FM) is the GPX BC112B at $26.49 at Target. It has no Bluetooth and no headphone jack. Paying $49.99 for the Jensen CD-560 adds Bluetooth input, but it takes 8 C batteries and, by a Target Q&A answer, has no radio presets. Above that, the Philips TAZ4300 ($69.99) and Panasonic SC-PM270 ($139.99) are FM only, and the Panasonic is sold out at Panasonic's own store. ChatGPT's Sony CFD-S70 card leads to a product the shopper can't easily buy new in the US: there was no listing at Target or Best Buy, and the one US offer we opened was a $159.99 refurbished unit. For a new unit under $50, the pick is the GPX or the Jensen CD-560, not the Sony.
